/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 02 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2648 (-66)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3963 (-163)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1874 (-15)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1856 (-9)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1014 (0)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market opened the week on a softer note, with the BCI 182 5TC dropping by $1,476 to $35,944. The Pacific saw a relatively busy start to the week, although increased fixing activity failed to prevent rates from coming under pressure. The C5 index slipped by $1.080 to $13.80, while C3 dipped by $0.235 to $36.560. In the Pacific, two miners were active in the market, with offers initially heard in the mid-$14s. However, with bids sitting in the mid-$13s, owners showed limited resistance as reports emerged of around 8–10 fixtures concluded in the region of $13.80. The volume of fixing activity provided some support to market liquidity, although the softer levels reflected a more cautious approach from charterers. Sentiment from South Brazil and West Africa to China was also a touch softer following a lacklustre start to the week. Activity remained very limited, with a lack of meaningful bids and a softening FFA market weighing on sentiment. Offers were reported around $37.50, depending on dates, although the absence of fresh enquiry left owners struggling to find support at these levels. The North Atlantic was a notable exception, with a modest uptick in rates following a firmer fixture on Friday. The C8 index nudged up by $1,218 to $32,531, while transatlantic offers were reported in the upper $30,000s as the week got underway.
PANAMAX
Participants noted a quiet start to the week with the market struggling to find meaningful support, particularly in the Atlantic, where a lack of fresh business and readily available tonnage continued to weigh on earnings. Trans-Atlantic trading remained notably slow, with little indication of Charterers needing to act quickly. Brokers commented that the tonnage count, particularly off the North Continent, is less extensive than the previous week but with demand for trans-Atlantic employment remaining significantly low, Owners are said to be weighing up a variety of alternatives, including fronthaul business loading further south. Fronthaul prospects offered a little more stability to the equation, with market sources noting some improvement in demand from EC South America and rates showing signs of responding accordingly. However, with the week still in its early stages, it remains to be seen whether this improvement can be sustained. The Ruby Star (79,263 2011) open Fujairah 13 October was placed on subjects for a trip via EC South America to the Red Sea at $19,000 plus $900,000 ballast bonus, although no other details were heard. In the Pacific, mineral demand from Australia is said to be holding steady, with some participants highlighting a widening bid-offer spread as Charterers are described as testing lower levels. North Pacific and Indonesian demand, by comparison, is said to be slipping, with market fundamentals described as increasingly imbalanced. The P5TC declined by $132 to settle at $16,867.
SUPRAMAX
A negative start to the new week with the 11TC average down $111 to settle at $23,458. All of the Atlantic routes remain under pressure following on from last week, but there was also concern in the Indian Ocean, with a source suggesting the market via South Africa to the Far East is in free fall. The Pacific market continues to buck the trend with continued positive sentiment in the North driven by NoPac and backhauls, whilst the south remains steady. The Medi Atlantico (60,550 2016) was said to have fixed basis delivery Tilbury for a trip to the East Mediterranean with scrap to Vianova, with the rate reported around $36,000 to $36,500, but could not be confirmed. In the East the Yong Xing 5 (52,803 2012) Bunati 31 October fixed to ESM for a trip to Shanghai/North China at somewhere in the mid $19,000’s.
HANDYSIZE
The Handysize market opened the week quietly, with limited visible activity and little fresh information emerging across both basins. In the Continent and Mediterranean, trading remained subdued, with largely unchanged fundamentals offering no clear catalyst for movement. The South Atlantic and US Gulf began on a softer footing, as lengthy tonnage lists weighed on sentiment and pushed rates below recently concluded levels. A 39,000-dwt vessel open Bejaia on 1–4 November was fixed for a fronthaul trip in the mid-$20,000s, while a 30,000-dwt vessel open Santos on 29–31 October was fixed from Recalada for a fronthaul trip at $15,000. Further details were not disclosed. Across Asia, activity was similarly muted, with limited fresh enquiry keeping the market broadly flat. Rates were generally discussed in line with last week’s levels, with little sign of a meaningful shift in the cargo-to-tonnage balance. Reflecting the subdued regional tone, the 7TC average edged down by $12 to close at $18,243.

Market Fundamentals
China’s Manufacturing PMI

China’s manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) fell 0.8 points from the prior month to a three-month low of 49.3 in October, standing below the 50-mark and indicating contraction, National Bureau of Statistics show.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape came under heavy pressure during the morning, with Nov and Dec falling sharply before recovering some ground into the close. Nov opened at 36,000 before dropping to 34,450, with heavy volume concentrated around 34,500, last trading at 34,850. Dec weakened from 36,000 to 34,750 before recovering to 35,350. Q1 27 traded heavily at 27,500, with several large blocks clearing, while Q2 27 traded between 32,450–32,500, including a 180-lot print at 32,450. Cal 27 eased from 31,000 to 30,850, while Cal 28 weakened from 27,100 to 26,900 before recovering to 27,000. Overall, Cape finished weaker across the curve, with main volume at the lower levels despite some late recovery in the front months.

PMX
PMX staged a strong recovery throughout the session, with Nov and Dec reversing early weakness as buying momentum improved into the afternoon.
